rationale: Comprehensive cohort evaluations of KDM2B-associated neurodevelopmental disorder (OMIM #621474) substantiate that KDM2B CxxC zinc finger domain variants display complete penetrance for neurodevelopmental delay and intellectual disability with a consistent facial gestalt, whereas predicted loss-of-function (pLOF) variants, 12q24.31 microdeletions, and JmjC domain missense variants demonstrate incomplete penetrance (neurodevelopmental impairment reported in only approximately 50% of carriers) along with marked variable expressivity and unaffected carrier parents.

evidence.text: CxxC domain variants show a highly penetrant phenotype with distinct facial gestalt, whereas loss-of-function and JmjC domain variants show incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity, with developmental delay or intellectual disability present in only about half of affected individuals.

new_directions.question_text: Does dominant-negative interference with non-canonical Polycomb repressive complex 1 (PRC1.1) assembly specifically drive the 100% penetrant CxxC phenotype compared to simple haploinsufficiency?
